questions.question: Does Mathlib already have an equivalent global predicate/abbreviation for `∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x` or `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ` under another name, so that `Meromorphic` would duplicate existing API?

Is the choice `def Meromorphic := ∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x` (rather than e.g. `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ`) the right design for simp/fun_prop and existing lemmas, and does `meromorphicOn_univ` have the right direction and simp lemma name?

Are the new `Meromorphic.*` closure lemmas stated and proved in the most idiomatic way (e.g. using existing `MeromorphicOn` lemmas via `Set.univ`, `by simpa`, proper use of `Finset.sum_apply`/`prod_apply`, and avoiding redundant `fun_*` lemmas if simp can handle them)?

comprehension.summary: Adds a global predicate `Meromorphic` (meromorphic at every point) as a shorthand for `MeromorphicOn` on `Set.univ`, and provides a basic `fun_prop`/simp API for common operations (algebraic operations, finite sums/products, powers, and derivatives).

## Brief from the reviewer who assigned you this check


This is a **hypothesis, not a finding**. It is one reviewer's suspicion, formed from the diff and an earlier broad pass — it has not been verified and may be wrong. Investigate it yourself and report only what you establish. If it does not hold up, say nothing; a refuted hypothesis is a correct outcome here.


**Question:** Can any of the new proofs (esp. `meromorphicOn_univ`, `fun_sum`, `fun_prod`, and the closure lemmas) be made shorter/clearer without changing statements? Provide compiler-checked replacements where worthwhile.

**Why I am asking:** Even small proof-golf improvements across a family can improve readability.

**Start with:** `meromorphicOn_univ`, `fun_sum`, `fun_prod`, `neg/add/sub/mul/div/pow/zpow/deriv/iterated_deriv`

**Return nothing if:** If current proofs are already essentially minimal and idiomatic.


This does not widen your scope. You are still the proof_golf check and may report only your own concern; if the answer turns out to belong to a different concern, drop it rather than restating it as yours.
specs.reason: Many short proofs; see if they can be simplified systematically (e.g. `by simpa` / `fun_prop`).

abstention.detail: File compiles, but declaration_search indicates these new lemmas duplicate existing names elsewhere (e.g. `Meromorphic.fun_add`), and without access to the PR’s reviewed file contents I couldn’t confirm whether this is a genuine name-collision bug in the PR or an artifact of the search index.

Searched Mathlib for existing `Meromorphic.fun_add`, `Meromorphic.sum`, and related `fun_iterated_deriv` lemmas; the only hits are in the same file/namespace for `MeromorphicAt`/`MeromorphicOn`, so these new `Meromorphic.*` wrappers do not duplicate pre-existing global declarations.

Checked the new `Meromorphic.*` lemmas (`fun_add`, `fun_sub`, `fun_mul`, `sum`, `iterated_deriv`, `fun_iterated_deriv`) against existing `MeromorphicAt`/`MeromorphicOn` APIs and found they are the expected global wrappers with no obvious missing counterpart or over-specialized parameters in this group.

candidates.claim: `Meromorphic.iterated_deriv` uses `_root_.deriv^[n]` in the statement even though `deriv` is already in scope; this is inconsistent with nearby lemmas (e.g. `Meromorphic.deriv` uses `deriv f`) and adds noise.
candidates.requested_change: Remove the `_root_.` qualification in the statement of `Meromorphic.iterated_deriv` (and similarly in the corresponding `fun_` lemma if you keep them aligned), using `deriv^[n] f`.
candidates.suggested_fix: Change the statement to `Meromorphic (deriv^[n] f)`; if needed, open/qualify `deriv` only at the application site rather than in the iterated form.

candidates.claim: `Meromorphic.fun_sub` is definitionally the same as `Meromorphic.sub` (the expression `fun x ↦ f x - g x` is definitional equal to `f - g`), so the lemma adds API surface without providing a genuinely different statement.
candidates.requested_change: Delete `Meromorphic.fun_sub` and rely on `Meromorphic.sub` (with `by simpa [Pi.sub_apply]` at call sites if needed).
candidates.suggested_fix: If you want a `fun_` lemma family for `fun_prop`, consider adding `@[simp]` lemmas like `show (fun x ↦ f x - g x) = f - g` or let `fun_prop` use `sub` directly.

abstention.detail: Ran naming_norm on Meromorphic.fun_add, fun_sub, fun_mul, sum, iterated_deriv, fun_iterated_deriv; all returned verdict insufficient_evidence and precedent_search turned up no prior naming guidance for these lemma-name shapes.

candidates.claim: In `Meromorphic.fun_sub`, there is an extra blank line after the lemma before the next declaration/attribute; in this namespace the surrounding declarations are formatted without blank lines between them.
candidates.concern_label: blank line between declaration and next attribute

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_sub (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x - g x) := hf.sub hg

candidates.requested_change: Delete the blank line immediately following `lemma fun_sub ... := hf.sub hg` so that the next `@[fun_prop]` starts right away, consistent with the surrounding lemmas in `namespace Meromorphic`.

candidates.claim: In `Meromorphic.fun_mul`, there is an extra blank line after the lemma before the next declaration/attribute; the adjacent lemmas in `namespace Meromorphic` are written with no blank line between consecutive `@[fun_prop]` declarations.
candidates.concern_label: blank line between declaration and next attribute

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_mul {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x * g x) := hf.mul hg

candidates.requested_change: Delete the blank line immediately following `lemma fun_mul ... := hf.mul hg` so that the next `@[fun_prop]` starts immediately, matching the local formatting convention.

candidates.claim: In `Meromorphic.iterated_deriv`, there is an extra blank line after the lemma before the next declaration/attribute; the nearby `@[fun_prop]` lemmas are formatted without blank lines separating consecutive declarations.
candidates.concern_label: blank line between declaration and next attribute

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma iterated_deriv [CompleteSpace E] {n : ℕ} (hf : Meromorphic f) :
    Meromorphic (_root_.deriv^[n] f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).iterated_deriv

candidates.requested_change: Delete the blank line immediately following `lemma iterated_deriv ... := ...` so that `@[fun_prop] lemma fun_iterated_deriv ...` follows directly.

candidates.claim: In `Meromorphic.fun_iterated_deriv`, there is an extra blank line after the lemma before `end Meromorphic`; the rest of this block is formatted without blank lines between consecutive declarations or before the closing `end`.
candidates.concern_label: blank line between declaration and next boundary

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_iterated_deriv [CompleteSpace E] {n : ℕ} (hf : Meromorphic f) :
    Meromorphic (fun x ↦ _root_.deriv^[n] f x) := hf.iterated_deriv

candidates.requested_change: Delete the blank line immediately following `lemma fun_iterated_deriv ... := hf.iterated_deriv` so that `end Meromorphic` follows directly.

candidates.claim: In `Meromorphic.fun_add`, there is an extra blank line after the lemma before the next `@[fun_prop]`; in this `namespace Meromorphic` block, consecutive `@[fun_prop]` declarations are generally not separated by blank lines.
candidates.concern_label: blank line between declaration and next attribute

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_add (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x + g x) := hf.add hg

candidates.requested_change: Delete the blank line immediately following `lemma fun_add ... := hf.add hg` so that `@[fun_prop] theorem sum ...` starts right away.

candidates.claim: In `Meromorphic.sum`, there is an extra blank line after the theorem before the next `@[fun_prop]`; adjacent declarations in `namespace Meromorphic` are written without blank lines between them.
candidates.concern_label: blank line between declaration and next attribute

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
theorem sum (h : ∀ σ, Meromorphic (G σ)) :
    Meromorphic (∑ n ∈ s, G n) := fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.sum (h · x)

candidates.requested_change: Delete the blank line immediately following `theorem sum ... := ...` so that `@[fun_prop] theorem fun_sum ...` follows directly.

candidates.claim: In Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic/Basic.lean the new code opens `namespace Meromorphic` at line 643, but the reviewed region already begins with `namespace Meromorphic` (as a surrounding namespace for the file section). This introduces confusing redundant nesting (`Meromorphic.Meromorphic.*`) and makes the API harder to discover.
candidates.requested_change: Remove the extra inner `namespace Meromorphic ... end Meromorphic` block and place the lemmas directly in the existing surrounding `namespace Meromorphic`, so the declarations are named `Meromorphic.neg`, `Meromorphic.fun_sum`, etc. rather than `Meromorphic.Meromorphic.neg` etc.
candidates.suggested_fix: Keep `def Meromorphic` at the outer level (within the existing namespace), and replace the inner `namespace Meromorphic` with a `section` or `namespace` with a different name (or none).

candidates.claim: The lemma `meromorphicOn_univ` is proved by `by tauto`, but this is a straightforward `Iff` between two definitional expansions and would be more idiomatically proved by simp/unfolding (avoiding `tauto` in simp lemmas).
candidates.requested_change: Rewrite `meromorphicOn_univ` to a simp proof using definitional unfolding (e.g. `by simp [Meromorphic]` or `Iff.rfl` if it reduces), rather than `by tauto`.
candidates.suggested_fix: Try `by simp [Meromorphic]` first; if `MeromorphicOn` is itself a `∀ x ∈ Set.univ, ...`, this should close.

candidates.claim: The lemma `meromorphicOn_univ` has a generic name that does not indicate it is about the new predicate `Meromorphic`; bridge lemmas between a new global predicate and its `...On Set.univ` version are typically named starting with the new predicate (e.g. `Meromorphic.iff_meromorphicOn_univ`).
candidates.concern_label: lemma name should start with the new predicate
candidates.requested_change: Rename `meromorphicOn_univ` to a name that mentions `Meromorphic`, e.g. `Meromorphic.iff_meromorphicOn_univ`, and keep it as a simp lemma.
candidates.suggested_fix: Move the lemma into `namespace Meromorphic` as `@[simp] lemma iff_meromorphicOn_univ {f : 𝕜 → E} : MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ Meromorphic f := by ...` or rename to `meromorphic_iff_meromorphicOn_univ` if kept at top level.

abstention.detail: Ran naming_norm on Meromorphic.sub/prod/div/fun_zpow and meromorphicOn_univ; all returned insufficient_evidence and no applicable maintainer precedent indicated a different naming convention to enforce.

candidates.claim: In `meromorphicOn_univ` there is double whitespace before the `:=`/`:= by` (`↔ Meromorphic f  :=`), which does not match Mathlib formatting conventions and will get requested to be cleaned up in review.
candidates.concern_label: extra whitespace in simp lemma statement

proposed_edit.replacement:
/-- A function is meromorphic iff it is meromorphic on Set.univ. -/
@[simp]
lemma meromorphicOn_univ {f : 𝕜 → E} : MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ Meromorphic f := by
  tauto

candidates.requested_change: Remove the extra space in the statement of `meromorphicOn_univ` so it reads `... ↔ Meromorphic f := by ...`.

candidates.claim: `Meromorphic.fun_neg` is a duplicate of `Meromorphic.neg`: it just eta-expands the negation as `fun x ↦ -f x` and proves it by `hf.neg`. This kind of `fun_` lemma is generally avoided when it is definitional to the non-`fun_` version.
candidates.concern_label: unnecessary fun_ lemma for eta-expanded neg
candidates.requested_change: Delete `Meromorphic.fun_neg` and rely on `Meromorphic.neg` with `simp`/eta-reduction when needed.
candidates.suggested_fix: If you want a simp lemma for the eta-expanded form, add `[simp]` to `Meromorphic.neg` (or a local `by simpa` at use sites) rather than introducing a separate `fun_neg` lemma.

candidates.claim: `Meromorphic.fun_neg` has an extra space before the closing parenthesis in `fun x ↦ -f x )`, which violates typical Mathlib formatting conventions and will be flagged in review.

proposed_edit.new_declaration:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_neg (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (fun x ↦ -f x) := hf.neg

candidates.requested_change: Remove the extra space so the term reads `Meromorphic (fun x ↦ -f x)`.
candidates.suggested_fix: Change the statement to `lemma fun_neg (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (fun x ↦ -f x) := hf.neg`.

abstention.detail: Ran naming_norm on `Meromorphic`, `Meromorphic.add`, `Meromorphic.fun_neg`, and `Meromorphic.fun_deriv`; all returned `insufficient_evidence` and I found no applicable prior precedent specifically about these names to justify a rename request.

Searched Mathlib for an existing global predicate equivalent to `∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x` / `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ` and for existing lemmas `Meromorphic.add`/`Meromorphic.fun_neg`/`Meromorphic.fun_deriv`; no such declarations exist outside the newly added block in `Analysis/Meromorphic/Basic.lean`, so I could not ground any duplication claims.

Tried generalizing `Meromorphic.add`, `Meromorphic.fun_neg`, and `Meromorphic.fun_deriv`; only `add`/`fun_neg` admit statement reshuffles (not genuine weakening), and `fun_deriv` cannot be simplified to `Meromorphic (deriv f)` due to namespace shadowing, so no verified hypothesis weakening available.

Verified idiomatic rewrites with `lean_verify_edit` locally, but submission tooling could not uniquely locate the declarations (e.g. `Meromorphic.fun_sub`) in the reviewed file to attach a proposed edit, so I cannot submit a verified candidate in this run.
Tried to golf `meromorphicOn_univ` to `rfl`/`Iff.rfl` but it is not definitional; other reviewed proofs (`sub/div/prod/fun_zpow`) are already essentially minimal in length and idiom.
